plan.analysis: Baseline constant steps give R=2/3. A Gaussian f has Gaussian f*f and R=1/sqrt(2)=0.707106..., strictly better, so the seed is not optimal. The main bet is that local nonparametric optimization from a Gaussian-like seed can beat the Gaussian and find the true shape; a parametric generalized-Gaussian scan gives a safe high baseline and tests tail exponent; a low-dimensional symmetric random evolution tests whether a flatter compact profile beats Gaussian.

experiments.hypothesis: A discretized Gaussian already beats the constant, and projected local optimization of its step heights will find a profile with R above 1/sqrt(2).
experiments.change: In construct set N=201 and initialize h_i=exp(-((i-100)/25)^2). Maximize the exact R(h) computed from np.convolve(h,h) and the knot formula using scipy.optimize.minimize(method='L-BFGS-B', bounds=[(0,None)]*N, jac='2-point'). After each convergence, restart from the best h multiplied by 1+0.05*N(0,1) noise (then clip and renormalize sum to 1). Keep the global best and continue until 28 s of process_time. Return the best h.
experiments.prediction: The returned score will exceed 0.7070, likely 0.708-0.72, and the best h will be a smooth unimodal profile near Gaussian but slightly modified.

experiments.hypothesis: The generalized Gaussian family exp(-|t/s|^p) contains the R=1/sqrt(2) Gaussian at p=2; scanning p tests whether a different tail exponent gives a better autoconvolution concentration.
experiments.change: Set N=4001 on t in [-1,1]. Scan p in np.linspace(1,4,61) and log-spaced s in [0.03,0.5] with 40 values, forming h=exp(-|t/s|^p). Compute exact R via np.convolve(h,h) and the given knot formula. Refine around the best (p,s) on a finer grid, then increase N to 8001 and refine again if time allows. Spend up to 28 s of process_time refining and return the best h found.
experiments.prediction: The optimum will be near p=2 with score about 0.7071; any p deviating significantly from 2 will score lower, confirming Gaussian as the best in this family.

experiments.hypothesis: A compactly supported, symmetric profile with a flatter top than Gaussian may have a positive-definite autoconvolution with higher L2/Linf ratio; a low-dimensional search can discover this without relying on pixel gradients.
experiments.change: Set N=401. Parameterize a symmetric profile by K=15 control heights on the left half and center, interpolate to N with np.interp, and make it symmetric. Initialize controls from a Gaussian with sigma=0.15*N. Run a (1+1)-evolution: copy controls, mutate all log-heights by N(0,sigma_m) with sigma_m=0.3, accept if R improves; every 2000 steps multiply sigma_m by 0.95, and every 5000 steps occasionally restart from the best with sigma_m=0.5. Use process_time until 28 s and return the best interpolated h.
experiments.prediction: If Gaussian is locally/globally optimal, the score will stay near 0.707; if a flatter compact profile is better, this search will return a score visibly above 0.7071, with a more plateau-like f.

plan.analysis: p0006 shows that stochastic multiscale block search around a dense N=50 shape improves strongly to 0.833, while p0005 shows projected L-BFGS can find sparse high-scoring shapes (0.821). The Gaussian/parametric branches are clearly weaker. I bet the best shape is a smooth asymmetric dense profile near p0006, and that systematic local optimization at multiple resolutions will squeeze out more. In parallel, sparse-support optimization from p0005 tests whether zeros plus support editing can beat the dense line. Spread bets: one L-BFGS refinement, one deterministic coordinate/pattern search, one sparse-support branch.

experiments.hypothesis: p0006 is a good basin; exact-R L-BFGS-B on log-heights, initialized from p0006 and its upsampled versions, will refine it more efficiently than random block perturbations.
experiments.change: Set best=start. For N in [50,100,200,400], upsample best to N with np.interp. Parameterize x=log(h+1e-12), run scipy.optimize.minimize on -R(exp(x)) with method='L-BFGS-B', bounds=[(-20,10)]*N, jac='2-point', options maxiter=2000. After each run, keep the result if R improves. Then perform 5 random restarts per N by perturbing log x with Gaussian sigma 0.05, 0.1, 0.2 and rerun L-BFGS-B. Return best when time is nearly exhausted.
experiments.prediction: The score will exceed 0.833, likely in 0.840-0.860, and the best N will be >=50 with a smooth asymmetric profile; if no N improves, p0006 is near a local optimum.

experiments.hypothesis: A deterministic full coordinate/pattern search, rather than random blocks, will find better height adjustments around p0006 and confirm whether N=50 or a finer discretization is best.
experiments.change: Start from start. For N in [50,75,100,150], resample start to N. Repeat sweeps over all indices i: for each i test multiplicative factors [0.5,0.7,0.85,0.95,1.05,1.15,1.4,2.0] on h[i] and additive shifts +/-0.01,0.03,0.1 times current mean; accept the single best change for that i immediately. After each full sweep, also try block moves on adjacent pairs (i,i+1) with a 5x5 grid of multiplicative factors around 1. Stop a sweep when no improvement; then move to next N and keep global best. Use all remaining time.
experiments.prediction: Score will rise above 0.833, likely 0.838-0.855, and the best N may shift above 50 if the coarse steps were limiting.

experiments.hypothesis: p0005's sparse support is a genuinely different high-scoring regime; alternating support editing with L-BFGS on nonzero entries can improve it and possibly beat the dense p0006 line.
experiments.change: Start from start (p0005 construction). Maintain support mask S = h > 1e-8*max(h). Loop: run L-BFGS-B on x=log(h[S]) with objective -R(h), bounds [(-20,10)]; then for each zero index and each smallest nonzero index, test setting that entry to 0.1*mean(h) or 0, run a short L-BFGS-B on the new support, and accept the best support change if R improves. Also test adding a new support point at the midpoint of the largest zero gap. Repeat until time nearly exhausted; return global best.
experiments.prediction: p0005 will improve from 0.821 to at least 0.83, and may exceed 0.833 if sparse/asymmetric support is optimal; otherwise best remains p0006, confirming the dense branch.
